text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 1.6% today after jumping sharply over the prior two days, as crude oil prices retreated from their recent highs. U.S. crude dropped back below $98 a barrel on October 15th as traders digested new supply developments—the International Energy Agency announced it would release over 20 million barrels of diesel to ease record-high U.S. prices, which countered the bullish impact of Iran's escalating attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. For a refiner like Marathon, lower crude prices compress profit margins on refined products, even though the company benefits from higher throughput when refineries run at elevated capacity (currently 92.7%).

The stock's pullback today sits within a broader two-week rally driven by geopolitical risk premiums and tight diesel supplies that had pushed crude and refined product prices higher. With diesel inventories unusually low and Middle East tensions supporting prices through mid-week, the announcement of emergency diesel releases from strategic reserves undercut the supply-crunch story that had fueled the prior gains.
